name: Olympus Mons caldera
summary: The summit caldera of the largest volcano on Mars, with the USGS geologic map of its six paterae.

frame.note: x = R cos(lat_c) dlon, y = R dlat on the 3,396,190 m sphere; east-west scale error within +/-0.6 % across the map

grid.note: HRSC/MOLA blended DEM at its native 0.0034 degree (about 200 m) posts

layers.name: Relief
layers.note: HRSC/MOLA blend 200 m, hillshade (3x) over elevation colour

layers.name: Slope
layers.note: Slope over 200 m; caldera walls are steeper over shorter distances than this grid can show

layers.name: Geologic units (USGS SIM 3470)
layers.note: Unit polygons from the 1:200,000 map; dark lines are mapped faults, pale lines ridge crests

legend.name: Zeus Patera floor
legend.desc: Caldera floor; highest near the east wall, lowest in the centre

legend.name: Hera Patera floor
legend.desc: Caldera floor; formed after Zeus Patera

legend.name: Hermes and Dionysus Paterae floor
legend.desc: Two connected depressions west of Zeus Patera; radial ridges

legend.name: Athena Patera floor
legend.desc: Near-circular 20 × 22 km pit at the northeast of the caldera

legend.name: Apollo Patera floor
legend.desc: 12 × 16 km pit at the southwest end; the deepest wall (about 2.9 km)

legend.name: Undifferentiated summit lava flows
legend.desc: Oldest surface unit, covering most of the summit

legend.name: Differentiated lava flows
legend.desc: A few hundred flows with mappable lobate margins radiating from the caldera

legend.name: Caldera wall material
legend.desc: Layered rock exposed in the caldera walls (unit Aow in the pamphlet)

legend.name: Pangboche crater floor
legend.desc: Hummocky floor with blocks up to about 150 m

legend.name: Pangboche crater wall and rim
legend.desc: Layered upper walls; ejecta blocks up to about 70 m on the rim

checks.name: Highest point against the published MOLA value
checks.note: SIM 3470 (MOLA): the volcano's highest point is 21,290 m and lies outside the caldera; this compares the blend with that value, it does not validate either.

checks.name: Caldera floor elevations by patera
checks.note: From the blend within each mapped unit; SIM 3470 describes Zeus Patera's floor as about 18,000 m at its centre and 19,500 m near the east wall.

sources.name: Mars HRSC MOLA Blended DEM Global 200 m v2
sources.producer: USGS Astrogeology (Fergason et al., 2018), from Mars Express HRSC and MGS MOLA

sources.name: Geologic map of Olympus Mons caldera (SIM 3470)
sources.producer: Mouginis-Mark, P.J., 2021, Geologic map of Olympus Mons caldera, Mars: U.S. Geological Survey Scientific Investigations Map 3470, scale 1:200,000, https://doi.org/10.3133/sim3470

capabilities.name: Elevation, 3D caldera
capabilities.detail: HRSC/MOLA blend at 200 m posts over the 1:200,000 map area.

capabilities.name: Slope and elevation profiles
capabilities.detail: Over 200 m only. Caldera walls 1–3 km high are steeper over shorter distances than this shows.

capabilities.name: Surface pressure
capabilities.detail: Mars Climate Database v6.2 only; no pressure has been measured above about 4 km anywhere on Mars. A ±10 % assumption band is shown.

capabilities.name: GCR dose estimate
capabilities.detail: Effective dose, dose equivalent and water-phantom absorbed dose from published AtRIS/Geant4 tables; the paper's 82 Pa case is the top of Olympus Mons. No measurement exists here.

capabilities.name: Dose differences across the caldera
capabilities.detail: Hydrostatic pressure from the DEM; the modeled change across the caldera is below the model's Monte Carlo noise.

capabilities.name: Terrain shielding of dose
capabilities.detail: No zenith-angle resolution in the published tables, and a 200 m grid cannot locate person-scale shelter.

capabilities.name: RAD-E comparison, walking routes
capabilities.detail: No RAD-equivalent model at 2–3 g/cm2; the 200 m grid cannot represent hazards at the scale of a person.
